For patients with HER2-positive early breast cancer and residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy, escalating adjuvant treatment improves outcomes. In high-risk patients, DESTINY-Breast05 found that trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) reduced the 3-year risk of recurrence compared with trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1). T-DXd also carries a risk of fatal interstitial lung disease (ILD). The US FDA approval for adjuvant T-DXd includes all patients with residual disease, including lower-risk patients not represented in the trial. We used decision modeling to project 10-year survival across recurrence-risk groups to aid in clinical decision-making.
